title: Fractal Analytics Ltd - 544700 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Fractal Q4 FY26 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR 886 crore (USD 97m) with Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin at 22.1%, while FY26 TMT weakness cut full-year growth to 19%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 886 crore, up 17% YoY and 4% QoQ, or 10% YoY in constant currency. FY26 revenue grew 19% to INR 3,300 crore, with management saying TMT client issues cost roughly 8 points of growth (27% ex-TMT). Margins expanded: Q4 gross margin 48.2% and adjusted EBITDA 22.1%, though about 147 bps of Q4 EBITDA came from a UK grant and variable pay true-ups that may not recur. The company repaid its long-term debt after March 31, 2026 using IPO proceeds and is now debt-free.

financial_highlights.change: +30% YoY; INR 357 crore (+43%) excluding associate losses

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,052 crore (USD 219 million), incl. INR 957 crore IPO proceeds

segments.name: Healthcare and life sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 66% for the year and is now the second-largest vertical on a quarterly run-rate basis.

segments.name: CPG and retail
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at 37% of revenue; grew 12% for the year, held back by first-half weakness after tariff-related freezes.

segments.name: Technology, media and telecom (TMT)
segments.commentary: Declined 1% for the year and 19% in Q4 on client-specific issues: a JV that moved work away, a client restructuring, and data-led delays on a large MAG7 engagement.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Europe grew 34% and Americas 20% for FY26; APAC declined 3% for the year, turning to 7% growth in Q4.

segments.name: Fractal Alpha (Asper.ai and Analytics Vidhya)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 41% in FY26 (Asper +31%, Analytics Vidhya +49%); segment loss narrowed to INR 15 crore from INR 26 crore in FY25 and INR 54 crore in FY23.

segments.name: Qure.ai (associate)
segments.commentary: Drag on profitability through FY26 after USAID-linked tuberculosis funding dried up; management says it now has a strong order pipeline as of April 2026, but gave no figures.

guidance_outlook: No specific revenue guidance; management expects historical growth rates to be a good indication for FY27.
Expects TMT client-specific issues to work through during FY27, with TMT to do better in the next few quarters.
Targets output, outcome or licence-based revenue at 60% of total within two to three years, from about 20 points below that today.
Targets licence-driven revenue rising from about 3% of revenue to 20% by 2030, to expand gross margin.
Intends to keep expanding gross margin while growing faster, with operating leverage continuing; will keep investing in sales and R&D.
Expects CPG to do better overall in FY27 and expects improvement across verticals.
Expects Qure.ai to have much better revenue growth and to stop contributing additional losses to Fractal in FY27.
Q4 margin benefits from the UK grant and variable pay adjustments may or may not repeat.
capex_capacity: R&D spend was INR 212 crore in FY26, up 48% YoY; INR 134 crore (4.1% of revenue) was expensed in the P&L, and management cited R&D at 6.4% of revenue in its closing remarks.
SG&A rose 96 bps as a share of revenue in FY26 from relationship management investment and new office openings.

Restructured in April 2026 into one platform (Cogentiq) and three go-to-market pillars (AI-led transformation, AI foundations, AI for work and workforce transformation) across three regions (Americas, Europe, APAC).
Cogentiq is the agentic AI platform; a Mag7 technology company chose it after a three-month evaluation.
Launched Flyfish.ai agentic sales platform with 35 coordinated agents; Vaidya 2.0 healthcare foundation model is available with developer API access.
Fractal is debt-free after repaying long-term debt in April 2026 from IPO proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management said client-specific issues cut FY26 growth from 27% (ex-TMT) to 19% reported; excluding the top three client issues, the ex-TMT rate was roughly similar.
Output- and outcome-based pricing carries a 5 to 7 point gross margin premium over input-driven pricing; licence-driven revenue carries about 25 to 30 points more.
Account scope is USD 2m to USD 100m per client per year; Must Win Clients are defined as companies with USD 10bn revenue, USD 20bn market cap, or 30m customers.
Asper has about 15 CPG clients; Analytics Vidhya and Asper each serve 15+ clients.

Management reports growing enterprise AI demand but says friction remains as enterprises are still adopting AI for the first time, and cites geopolitical and trade uncertainty, including the Middle East conflict.

qa_highlights.question: What are the magnitude and nature of the TMT revenue drop?
qa_highlights.answer: One APAC TMT client moved its business into a JV, cutting the relationship sharply but not to zero. A restructuring enterprise software client also reduced spend. A MAG7 client's work was delayed by data readiness, reducing Q4 revenue recognised.

qa_highlights.question: Is TMT a low-margin vertical?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TMT is not low margin; gross margin is a couple of points below other verticals because of input-driven work, and net operating margin is robust.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is output-based, and what growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Fractal does not report this separately. It targets 60% output, outcome or licence-based revenue in two to three years, about 20 points above today. No revenue guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Cogentiq share of revenue and the 2030 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Cogentiq is still small. Licence-driven revenue, which includes Cogentiq, Asper and PiEvolve, is about 3% of revenue, with a target of 20% by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company reinvest in growth or protect profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to maximise revenue growth while holding a profitability threshold, and will not sacrifice gross margin for growth.

qa_highlights.question: How does Fractal approach a data-platform-plus-AI trend (Databricks, Snowflake)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees data platforms as partners and beneficiaries, but says an agentic layer like Cogentiq is also needed. It did not give an exact count of certified staff, saying there are hundreds per platform.

risks_watch: TMT: Q4 decline of 19% and client concentration risk; management expects recovery but gave no quantified timing.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA includes a UK grant and variable pay true-ups worth about 147 bps, which may not repeat.
Qure.ai: recovery depends on a pipeline that management has not quantified, and it has been a profit drag.
Working capital: receivables rose INR 86 crore in FY26; DSO improved to 72 days, but CFO conversion fell to 70% of adjusted EBITDA from 82%.
Pricing mix shift to output and licence contracts is a key margin driver; progress against the 60% and 20% targets should be tracked.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term enterprise AI opportunity and margin trajectory, but cautious on near-term specifics. Management gave no revenue guidance, and answers on TMT and Qure.ai were qualitative with few figures.
key_quotes: We do not have specific revenue guidance at this point in time, but we expect that our historical revenue growth rates are a good indication of where we should be growing in the next year as well.
Segment losses have continued to narrow from INR 26 crore in FY2025 to INR 15 crore in FY2026, even as we kept investing.

So the best really is if you can drive outcome or output-based deals with some license component built into them that is the best possible way to not only create large revenue growth, but also do it at a much higher gross margin overall.
That drag is getting lifted as we speak, and Qure will have a much better year and also not contribute to additional losses to Fractal.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management says historical growth rates (FY26 19% reported, 13% constant currency) are a good indication, with TMT expected to recover and Qure.ai losses to stop, but no specific capacity, orders or contracts with numbers were given to back it.
